key_insight: WASD improves knowledge distillation for LLMs by aligning teacher and student distributions with a Wasserstein distance that uses token embedding semantics instead of only vocabulary-index probabilities.
engineering_relevance: This offers a more semantically informed and computationally tractable distillation objective for building smaller, cheaper LLMs without adding extra networks.
method: Use a cost matrix derived from token embeddings to measure semantic distance between vocabulary tokens.
Optimize a Sinkhorn-divergence-based objective for tractable Wasserstein distillation.
Derive a gradient-equivalent formulation so the loss can be trained efficiently during LLM distillation.
evidence_signal: Across multiple LLM families and scales, the method reportedly improves distillation performance on instruction following, mathematical reasoning, and code generation tasks.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of token embeddings and the efficiency/stability of Sinkhorn optimization, which may add implementation sensitivity at scale.
paper_title: WASD: Wasserstein-based Knowledge Distillation for Large Language Models
